title: Koszul augmentation lifts without regularity
statement: For a commutative ring A, ideal I, finite tuple g in I and projective resolution P of A/I, there is a chain map from the Koszul complex of g to P whose degree-zero augmentation is I.mkQ composed with exteriorPower.zeroEquiv. The tuple need not generate I and need not be regular.

proof.text: Each Koszul term is an exterior power of a finite free module, hence projective. The degree-one boundary evaluated under zeroEquiv is the linear combination of the tuple elements, so the quotient augmentation kills it.

Lift the augmentation through P.pi in degree zero using Projective.factorThru. P.exact_0 lifts the first differential to degree one. In each subsequent degree the preceding chain-map equation and d squared equal to zero put the required map in the cycles; P.exact_succ and projectivity lift it one degree further. ChainComplex.mkHom assembles these maps and its degree-zero equation gives the requested augmentation.

lean.statement: theorem koszul_augmentation_lift_exists (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → I) (P : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I))) : ∃ a : ExteriorAlgebra.koszulComplex A r (fun j ↦ (g j : A)) ⟶ P.complex, a.f 0 ≫ P.π.f 0 = ModuleCat.ofHom (I.mkQ.comp (exteriorPower.zeroEquiv A (Fin r →₀ A)).toLinearMap)
